overview: The main story/world bosses in Once Human are known as 'The Great Ones' — massive creatures forged from people mutated by Stardust, each guarding a Monolith in a different region of Nalcott and requiring a team to defeat efficiently. Beyond the Great Ones, seasonal Visional Wheel content adds rotating bosses (e.g. the Riftwalker in the Gravity Abyss season) and events add limited-time bosses (e.g. the Block Wanderer).

greatOnes.name: Ravenous Hunter
greatOnes.mechanics: Destroy its Gatling weapon to disable its shield, then stun it and hit the yellow head weak spot.
greatOnes.drops: Burn-effect weapon mods (confirmed), plus early-game crafting materials and blueprint fragments.

verification.notes: Mechanics and location per community guides; its weapon-effect mod drop is independently confirmed. Phase/weak-point breakdown added from a dedicated boss-fight guide; still community-sourced, not an official strategy document.

weakPoints: Right arm / Minigun mount (destroying it severs the arm and stuns the boss)

phases.description: Take cover from Gatling fire and destroy the gun; it overheats periodically, opening a damage window. At ~1/3 health it becomes immune and teleports away.
Destroy two Spawners (east and west of the arena) producing Gnawers, while dodging rockets, to force the boss back.
The boss reappears with its Minigun; use the brief re-entry window and thrown Explosive Barrels to burst it down.
The boss switches to a Rocket Launcher with Missile Cluster homing-rocket attacks; save consumables/Deviant abilities for this phase.

greatOnes.name: Treant
greatOnes.mechanics: Destroy the surrounding vines first, target the female humanoid figure on its back, and dodge laser beams that telegraph with a red light.
greatOnes.drops: Wood/plant-themed crafting materials and blueprint fragments. (Its specific weapon-effect mod drop isn't confirmed by available sources.)

verification.notes: Mechanics and location per community guides; its weapon-effect mod drop is independently confirmed. Phase/weak-point breakdown added from a dedicated boss-fight guide; still community-sourced, not an official strategy document.

weakPoints: The glowing red 'woman' figure fused into its back/head — doubles damage when hit

phases.description: Three vines with glowing red weak spots must be destroyed before the boss can take damage at all.

Once all three vines are down, the boss is vulnerable for roughly two minutes before the vines regrow and the loop restarts. Cyst Seeds spawn during this window and can be broken for a temporary attack-negating safety dome.

greatOnes.name: Arachsiam
greatOnes.mechanics: Avoid web-cocoon and rush attacks; focus the purple pustules on its back for maximum damage.
greatOnes.drops: Mid-tier crafting materials and blueprint fragments. (Its specific weapon-effect mod drop isn't confirmed by available sources.)

verification.notes: Mechanics and location per community guides; its weapon-effect mod drop is independently confirmed. Phase/weak-point breakdown added from a dedicated boss-fight guide; still community-sourced, not an official strategy document.

weakPoints: Purple bulges on the spider's back (legs take reduced damage)

phases.description: The boss moves quickly around the arena; sustained-DPS or sniper weapons work best while kiting.

At roughly 60-70% health the boss climbs the arena's central stone and releases a damage-immune mist, spawning glowing purple spider eggs outside the arena that must be destroyed to break the immunity.

greatOnes.name: Rabizex
greatOnes.mechanics: Keep distance, use powerful weapons on its weak points, and prioritize evasion since its movements are hard to predict up close.
greatOnes.drops: Shrapnel and Bounce-effect weapon mods (confirmed), plus mid-to-late-tier crafting materials and blueprint fragments.

verification.notes: Mechanics and location per community guides; its weapon-effect mod drop is independently confirmed. Phase/weak-point breakdown added from a dedicated boss-fight guide; still community-sourced, not an official strategy document.

weakPoints: Head (exposed once the first health bar depletes)
Shoulders (appear after the head is first exposed)

phases.description: The boss shows no obvious weak point at full health; focus general damage while dodging its ranged Stardust attacks and the hard-to-avoid 'Oblivion' dive attack.
Once the first health bar is depleted, a true head sticks out as a critical weak point, followed by weak points on the shoulders.
The boss periodically shields itself; destroying scattered dark-matter spheres breaks the shield.
At low health the boss enters a frenzied state with stronger attacks, but its head becomes a consistently exposed weak spot.

greatOnes.name: Mensdevoran (The Forsaken Giant)
greatOnes.mechanics: Jump over hand-slam shockwaves, stay close to its body to dodge sweeping arm attacks, and target glowing weak spots as they appear.
greatOnes.drops: Endgame crafting materials and Advanced Gear Workbench blueprint fragments. (Its specific weapon-effect mod drop isn't confirmed by available sources.)

verification.notes: Mechanics and location per community guides; its weapon-effect mod drop is independently confirmed. Phase/weak-point breakdown added from a dedicated boss-fight guide; still community-sourced, not an official strategy document.

weakPoints: Right biceps — a single glowing weak point rotates between these locations

phases.description: The glowing weak point rotates across face/palms/belly/biceps as the boss uses Slam, Sweep, and a crying Tears attack (each telegraphed by a glow before it lands).
The weak point shifts to the hands only, the boss becomes more aggressive, and it summons Elite minions to distract the player(s).

greatOnes.arenaNote: Each of the arena's floor sections can absorb 3 hits from the boss's attacks before breaking and shrinking the arena — spreading out where its attacks land avoids this.

seasonalAndEventBosses.name: Riftwalker
seasonalAndEventBosses.context: Visional Wheel S4: Gravity Abyss (patch 2.4.1) — a massive aerial Deviant fought across zero-gravity floating islands.
seasonalAndEventBosses.drops: Abyssal Cores (epic/legendary/mythic), Abyssal Essence, and the Aero/Downstar mods.

verification.notes: Seasonal/event context per community + in-game announcement text.

seasonalAndEventBosses.name: Block Wanderer
seasonalAndEventBosses.context: Block Adventure event on Wish Island (patch 3.0.3, Aug 5–23 2026) — defeat blocky creatures and challenge this boss for morphed Deviation rewards.
seasonalAndEventBosses.drops: Morphed Deviations (Zapamander, Nutcracker and Dr. Teddy variants) plus Block Adventure event currency.

verification.notes: Seasonal/event context per community + in-game announcement text.

note: Great Ones drop core weapon-effect mod sets (confirmed for Ravenous Hunter → Burn and Rabizex → Shrapnel/Bounce) alongside crafting materials and blueprint fragments — cross-reference the Mods section for what each weapon effect actually does. Drop tables for Treant, Arachsiam and Mensdevoran weren't available in the sources used to compile this database.
